title: The Chimeling That Would Not Stop Splitting
story: Beneath a frozen lake lies a hall of singing salt crystals, and Clamorel has been smashing them for the echo. Mr 6 swings his sword — and the chimeling shatters into three identical chimelings, all giggling. Three strikes later, Mr 6 lowers his blade and starts to think instead: chimelings cannot bear a single pure hummed note.
question: Clamorel begins as 1 chimeling, and every strike turns each chimeling into 3. After Mr 6's 4 strikes, how many pure notes must he hum to silence them all, if one note silences exactly 9 chimelings?
solution: Track the tripling: 1 → 3 → 9 → 27 → 81 chimelings after 4 strikes.
praise: Following the tripling chain is the tough part, and that was good thinking — the last step was grouping that crowd into bunches of 9.
hint: Write the chain one strike at a time: 1, then 3, then... only then worry about the notes.
victory: Nine clear notes ring through the salt hall, and the eighty-one chimelings snap back into one slightly embarrassed chimeling, who now hums harmony for the crystals instead of smashing them.
imagePrompt: A cavern of glowing blue salt crystals crowded with dozens of tiny giggling bell-shaped creatures, while a small numeral 6 knight stands calmly with sword sheathed, mouth open in a shining hummed note, cool moonlit light.
